title: Orochia Ecosystem Architecture
source: generated from code by products/orochia/scripts/generate-docs.mjs — do not hand-edit

repositories.name: orochia
repositories.role: Consumer platform, creator studio & 4K HLS player
repositories.description: Direct-to-Bunny streaming with short-lived signed URLs, server-side access control, gateway-confirmed unlocks and an idempotent double-entry ledger.

repositories.name: orochia-admin
repositories.description: Administrative console for performer records, content reports and platform revenue.

repositories.name: orochia-design-system
repositories.description: Component library and tokens shared by the Orochia applications.

repositories.name: orochia-mobile
repositories.role: iOS and Android app over the same API
repositories.description: Stories, protected 4K playback, challenges and auctions on iOS and Android — native sessions in secure storage, the design system's tokens and the animated mark from npm.

modules.name: Payments & ledger
features: Constant-time webhook signatures, no lenient mode

apiEndpoints.summary: Every auction for operators (latest first, optionally by status): video, creator, price, bids, timing, outcome.
Cancels an auction that is open or awaiting its decision, with a recorded reason; the leading bid is released.
Creator accounts with their verification state; `?verified=false` lists the review queue.
Records the outcome of a creator's 18 U.S.C. § 2257 review.
A creator's 2257 document (`?ref=private/documents/<uuid>.<ext>`), for operators only; never cached.

Operator view of the Explorer — the proof that Orochia's AI runs on Orazaka: whether the engine is configured (its host, never its key), the circuit breaker, how many discoverable videos have a vector, and the latest calls to Orazaka with the run id Orazaka answered (find `embedding.run runId=…` in its logs).
Embeds the discoverable videos that have no vector yet, now (the scheduler does it every ten minutes).
Operator overview: money, catalogue, the three queues that need a human, and 12 months of revenue and reports.
Payout requests with their creator; `?status=` filters.
Advances a payout.
The platform for operators: environment, database (size, rows per table), migration history, whether a reset is allowed.
The database backups kept in private storage, newest first.
Backs the whole database up now (gzipped JSON of every table, in private storage).
Deletes a backup from private storage.
Downloads a backup file (`?download=1`), or describes it: tables, rows, migrations.

Factory reset: backs the database up first (unless asked not to), wipes it and rebuilds it from the migrations — development deployments only (DATABASE_ALLOW_RESET, never the indexed production), after the operator typed “reset <database>”. The operator and the owner are kept.
Content reports, newest first; `?status=` filters.
Moves a report through triage (open → in review → resolved).

Platform storage for operators: usage against the cap and alert thresholds, the plans, the largest accounts, the last reconciliation with Bunny, and the state of the abuse defences (rate-limit store, bot challenge).
Reconciles the storage counters with Bunny now (lists the Stream library; at most a few times an hour).
Sets an account's storage plan (a name of ABUSE_QUOTA_PLANS, or null for the default); its held uploads go online if they fit.
Every account (filter by `?role=`, `?suspended=`, `?q=`): role, verification and suspension state.

Suspends an account (it can no longer sign in, and its open sessions are refused on their next request; its open auctions are cancelled and their bids released), reinstates it, or changes its role (a new creator waits for the 2257 review).
Law 25 portability: everything held about an account, as one JSON document (never a password hash, a destination or a token).
Ends every session of an account without suspending it (a lost phone, a doubt): a session token issued before this moment opens nothing, on the web and in the app.
The catalogue for moderation: every video with its creator, state and open reports; `?state=removed` lists takedowns.
Takes a video down (DMCA, terms, a confirmed report) with a recorded reason — cancelling its auction — or restores it.
Lists auctions by tab: open, upcoming, ended (sold), bidding (yours) or selling (your own).
Puts one of the creator's ready videos up for auction (start, end, starting price, rights, how it ends).
The creator cancels their auction while nobody has bid; the video gets its previous visibility back.
An auction as the viewer sees it: price, minimum next bid, timing, recent bids (aliases), and their own standing.
Places a bid in Orochia credits; they are held while the bid leads and released when it is outbid.
The creator accepts the best bid (the video is sold to its bidder) or declines it (the credits go back).
Server-Sent Events of an auction: each bid (amount, alias, new end) and every change of state.
The public bot-challenge settings (provider and site key), or null when protected forms need no challenge.
E-mails a password-reset link (1 h) to the address, if an active account uses it.
Password login — a session cookie for the browser, a bearer token for a native app.

Signs out: the request's session token — a native app's bearer or the browser's cookie — is revoked on the server (krizaka/orochia#127), so no surviving copy of it opens the account again; the browser's cookie is cleared too.
The signed-in account (with whether its e-mail is verified), or `user: null`.
The provider's redirect: checks the state, exchanges the code, then signs in (linked account or same verified address) or sends a new person to complete their account.
Sends the browser to the provider's consent page (state + PKCE kept in a signed 10-minute cookie).
Creates the account of a new Google / Facebook sign-in after the person gives a date of birth (18+), certifies it and accepts the terms.
The provider sign-in waiting to become an account: what the completion form can prefill.

The public configuration the web app and the native app read: the sign-in providers this deployment offers (only those whose keys are configured) and whether sign-up is open (`signupEnabled` — `AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED`).

Opens a sign-up form: a signed form token (bound to this browser's device cookie, set here when missing — or, with `?client=native`, to the app's device id header) and the public bot-challenge settings — the form cannot be posted without them.
Creates an account (a member — creators are opened later, never an administrator), signs it in and e-mails the link that verifies its address — until then the account can do nothing else.
E-mails a new verification link to the signed-in account (the previous link stops working).
Sets a new password with the link's one-time token (1 h).
Whether a username is free (unique address orochia.com/@username), with a free one suggested when it is not.
Verifies an e-mail address with the link's one-time token (48 h); refreshes the session of that account — the cookie of a browser, or, for a native app's bearer session, a new `token` in the answer.
Catalogue statistics for administrators, from the database.
Lists challenges by tab: open, calls (open calls), done (delivered), inbox (yours to answer or deliver), mine, backing.

Opens a challenge: a creator's goal (pledges until the deadline, all or nothing), a request to one creator (the sender's offer is held at once; the creator has three days to answer) or an open call for any creator (the author's pot is held; creators apply and the author picks one).
A challenge as the viewer sees it: progress, deadlines, backers (aliases), applications and what the viewer may do.
The creator a request was sent to accepts it (and must deliver in time) or declines it (every pledge comes back).
A verified creator applies to take an open call, with a short note for its author.
The author of an open call picks one applicant, who now has the delivery window to make it.
The author withdraws an open challenge (a goal, a request not answered yet, an open call): every pledge comes back.
What the creator can deliver: their ready videos not used elsewhere, or the stories posted since they committed.
The creator delivers a video or a story: the backers' pledges are paid and they can watch it.
Pledges Orochia credits to an open challenge; they are held until it is delivered and come back if it is not.
A goal's creator starts it as soon as the goal is reached (pledging stops; the delivery window begins).
Server-Sent Events of a challenge: each pledge (amount, alias, new total) and every change of state.
Sends a contact request (accepted at once when the other person already asked).
Removes a contact or withdraws a request (either side).
Accepts or rejects a request addressed to you, or blocks the other person.
Lists the signed-in user's conversations: the other participant, last message, unread count and visible presence.
Starts or retrieves a conversation with a specified user.
Lists messages in a conversation (latest page, or `?before=<seq>` to scroll back) and marks the latest as read.
Sends a direct message in a conversation (idempotent per `clientId`: a retry answers the stored message).
Reports a message the account received: a compliance report naming it, with its text, triaged by operators.
Marks a conversation read up to a message (`upTo`, its `seq`; everything when absent): the sender sees "read".
Tells the other participant that the account is typing (or stopped) — live only, never stored.
The account's live stream (Server-Sent Events): messages, receipts, typing, unread count, notifications and the presence of its circle; resumes after `Last-Event-ID` (or `?after=<seq>`) without loss.
The account's unread messages, all conversations (the badge; kept live by the `unread` event of the stream).
Your earnings for a period (?period=30d|90d|12m|all): totals, views, each video's revenue, the trend by kind, the last 30 days of tips, payments and payouts.
Downloads your earnings as CSV (?kind=transactions|videos&period=…), for your accounting.
The signed-in creator's balance, lifetime earnings and payout history — from the ledger.
Requests a payout to your saved payout account (an encrypted snapshot is kept); balance checked and reserved atomically.
A creator's public page: profile, videos, the collections you may open and, signed in, how you relate to them.
Unfollows a creator.
Follows a creator; the follow stays PENDING until the creator approves it.

Explore: without a search, the discovery sections (trending this week, new, stories, creators to follow, open auctions, open challenges, tags); with `q` and/or `tag` (or `view=all`), videos (paged), creators and stories.
The feeds, a page at a time.
Creates a group (the caller is its owner); the members must be the caller's contacts (or, for a creator, approved fans).
Closes the group (owner): nobody writes any more.
The group: its name, the caller's role and mute, its members.
Renames the group (owner).
Revokes every open invite (owner).
A new invite link (owner): the token is shown once, and valid for a week.
Leaves the group (the owner leaving passes it on).
Adds members (owner): contacts, up to 50 in all.
Removes a member (owner).
Mutes the group for some hours (no push, no badge), or `hours: null` to unmute.
Joins a group with an invite token (`/messages/join/<token>`): the answer is the conversation to open.
Content reports.
Opens a creator space for a member: the same account becomes CREATOR, pending its 18 U.S.C. § 2257 review (uploads open once an operator verifies it).
Records your date of birth (18+) when the account has none yet; once set it cannot be changed here.
Lists the accounts blocked by the signed-in user.
Forgets one of the account's phones (sign-out, notifications turned off on the device).
Registers the phone the app runs on for push notifications (an Expo push token, moved if it served another account).
Your editor drafts (newest first), with a short-lived link to each original clip; expired ones are removed.
Keeps an edit as a draft: records its settings and returns a Tus session to send the original clip straight to Bunny.
Deletes one of your drafts with its clip and music.
One of your drafts, with a short-lived link to its original clip.
Saves new edit settings or form values on a draft (the clip is not sent again); it is kept longer.
Removes the music track of a draft.
The music track of one of your drafts (private: served to you only).
Keeps (or replaces) the music track of a draft — MP3, M4A, AAC, WAV or OGG up to 25 MB.
Tells that a draft's original clip is fully sent, so it can be opened again before Bunny finishes processing.
A creator approves a follower (opening followers-only videos to them) or removes them.
Lists the external OAuth providers linked to the signed-in account.
Unlinks a connected OAuth provider identity from the signed-in account.
Lists invitations sent by the signed-in user.
Sends an invitation to join Orochia to a friend or collaborator.
Your reusable audience lists (private to you), with their size.
Creates an audience list (names are unique per account).
Deletes one of your lists; the videos and collections it opened close to its members.
Renames one of your lists.
Removes someone from one of your lists (`?userId=`): what the list opened closes to them.
The people in one of your lists.
Adds an account to one of your lists by username (idempotent; the list stays private).
Your followers, the creators you follow, your contacts and pending requests.
Your notifications, newest first, 25 at a time (`before` = an ISO date to page back), with the unread count.
Marks notifications read: the ones listed, or all of them.
Where your earnings are sent — shown masked (e.g.
Saves (or replaces) where your earnings are sent; the details are checked and encrypted at rest.
Reads the signed-in user's own profile and settings (private fields included: e-mail, date of birth).
Updates the signed-in user's own profile and preferences (only the fields sent).
Your storage: space and video time used against your plan, uploads on hold, today's uploads and the per-file limits.
Your stories of the last 30 days — up, encoding or expired — with their figures.
The creator's tag suggestions for the publish form: the tags they used before (most used first) and the curated list.
Your Orochia credits: balance (and what is held behind your leading bids and challenge pledges), the packs you can buy, how you can pay for them, and your history.
Buys credits: returns the gateway's hosted checkout (card, Apple Pay, Google Pay — card details never reach Orochia); the gateway's signed webhook adds the credits.
Prometheus metrics, behind a bearer token (OBSERVABILITY_METRICS_TOKEN).
The ways a buyer can pay on this deployment: credits (the wallet), then the external gateways.
Platform revenue, computed from the ledger only (administrators).
Your playlists, most recently changed first.
Creates a playlist.
Deletes a playlist (owner only).
A collection and its videos, for a viewer its permission admits (others get a 404).
Renames a collection, edits its description or who may open it (owner only).
Removes a video from a playlist (owner only).
Adds a video at the end of a playlist (owner only, idempotent).
Collections other accounts invited you to.
The presence (online · away · offline with the time last seen) of up to 100 accounts — only those the rules let the account see (lib/presence-rules.ts); the others are absent from the answer.
The app's activity on one of its streams: `away` when the page is hidden or idle, `online` when the person is back.
The people of the account's circle who are online or away right now ("Online now" in Messages).
Reference content classifications and age ratings (Kids Safe, General, Teens, Mature, Adult).
Default avatar and banner presets users can choose without uploading custom files.
The search palette: creators, videos, stories and tags matching what is typed (full-text, accents ignored, word prefixes); with nothing typed, the newest videos and the popular tags.

The stories rail: one ring per creator with current stories you may see (yours first, then unseen), signed for you — `?creator=<username>` keeps that creator's ring only (a profile's story ring); with `?pending=1`, your own video stories too while they are processing (`state`).
Publishes an image story (24 h) from an image stored by /api/uploads (category "stories"); verified creators only.
Withdraws a story: its creator or an operator.
Changes who sees a live story (its creator only; a story delivered for a challenge keeps its backers).
A story's activity for its creator: views (accounts named, visitors counted), likes, tips and who sent them.
Removes your like (idempotent).
Likes a story you may see (idempotent).
Answers a story privately: a direct message to its creator, linked to the story (blocks and message privacy apply).
Tips a creator from one of their stories.
Counts a view of a story you may see — once per viewer, never the creator's own.
Starts a video story: records it and returns a Tus session straight to Bunny (stories collection).

apiEndpoints.access: session · role depends on the request
apiEndpoints.summary: Stores an avatar or a profile banner (any account), a thumbnail, a story image or a 2257 document (creators); size and type checked per kind.
Unblocks a previously blocked user.
Blocks or unblocks a user: toggles block state on POST.
What is deployed: the package version, the short commit and the environment (inlined at build).
The creator deletes their video (refused while it is in an auction, and for a video its challenge's backers paid for).
The creator edits their video (an auctioned or challenge video keeps its audience): title, description, visibility, unlock price, tags, comments open.
The auction a video is in (open, awaiting its decision or sold), as the viewer sees it; null when there is none.
The comments of a video you may watch, oldest first; removed ones keep their place without text.
Comments on a video you may watch, or replies to one of its comments.
Removes a comment: its author, the video's creator or an operator.
A video's public metadata and figures (and whether you liked it); the stream is only served by /stream.
A five-minute signed link to the video's MP4 file, for its author and for a buyer whose grant includes downloading.
Removes your like (idempotent).
Likes a video you may watch (idempotent).
Counts a share of a video you may watch; the shared link still enforces the video's access.
Authorises a viewer and returns a short-lived signed HLS URL (AGENTS.md §2.A).

The player says how much of a video a signed-in viewer watched when they left it (ADR-081): the share watched goes to Orazaka's analytics (`watch`), and leaving at once is a `SKIP` for the recommender.
Starts the purchase of a video unlock.
Bunny Stream encoding events (https://bunny.net/docs/stream/webhooks), signed v1 with the library's Read-Only API key (MEDIA_STREAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET).
Gateway payment notifications.

roles.title: Clients
roles.rule: what a person uses: the pages of apps/web (in the browser), a sibling app repository (admin console, mobile app)

roles.title: Application
roles.rule: the API route handlers of apps/web (app/api/**/route.ts): the one process that serves every client

roles.title: Packages
roles.rule: a workspace package of this monorepo (packages/*), imported by the application

roles.title: Design system
roles.rule: the Orochia design system and the @krizaka/* packages the apps install

roles.title: Data stores
roles.rule: a database an app opens (pg / Drizzle and its DATABASE_URL)

roles.title: External services
roles.rule: a third-party service the code calls (its API host appears in the sources)

modules.name: @krizaka/orochia-admin
modules.description: Operator console for Orochia: 2257 creator verification, content reports, payouts and treasury

modules.name: orochia-mobile
modules.description: Orochia for iOS and Android — the creator video platform, in your pocket. React Native (Expo).

modules.name: @orochia/web
modules.description: The web app in the browser: viewer pages, creator studio, the HLS player and the Tus uploader (Next.js App Router).

modules.name: @orochia/web
modules.description: The API: 145 route handlers — access control, signed media URLs, payments and the ledger, auctions, challenges, realtime. Deployed with the pages, one process.

modules.name: @orochia/config
modules.description: Shared TypeScript, ESLint and Tailwind presets of the workspace.

modules.name: @orochia/db
modules.description: PostgreSQL schema (Drizzle, the source of truth), migrations and migrator, connection pool, LISTEN/NOTIFY, development seed.

modules.name: @orochia/media
modules.description: Bunny Stream client, direct Tus signing, signed HLS playback tokens (300 s), webhook verification, upload limits.

modules.name: @orochia/payments
modules.description: Gateway adapters (CCBill, Segpay, NowPayments, Stripe), payment intents, exactly-once settlement, the double-entry ledger, credits, payouts, auctions and challenges.

modules.name: @krizaka/orochia-design-system
modules.description: The Orochia identity on the Krizaka platform: the Obsidian Velvet Noir theme as --kz-* token overrides and the product composites (StatusBadge, SocialIcon, orochiaButton), with their documentation registry (krizaka.com/docs/orochia/ui). The primitives come from @krizaka/ui.

modules.name: @krizaka/charts
modules.description: Krizaka's data visualisation: typed, declarative React charts (line, area, bar, pie, radar, heatmap, calendar, sankey, funnel, gauge, sparkline, candlestick, treemap, scatter, geo map, 3D globe) on the --kz-* tokens and the brand palettes — an accessible data table, a written summary and keyboard navigation in every chart, SSR without layout shift, and React Native for the simple types.

modules.name: @krizaka/i18n
modules.description: The i18n engine of every Krizaka app: typed message keys and placeholders from en.json, format(), plurals through @krizaka/intl, <Rich> (<b>, <a>), a React provider, and the krizaka-i18n CLI that checks catalogues and finds hard-coded strings.

modules.name: @krizaka/icons
modules.description: The Krizaka signature icons: one drawing language (24 grid, cut corners, a node at the core) for every Krizaka product — React (tree-shakable, server-safe) and React Native (react-native-svg).

modules.name: @krizaka/intl
modules.description: Money, numbers, dates and plurals formatted the same way in every Krizaka product: zero dependency, built on Intl, money from integer minor units only.

modules.name: @krizaka/push
modules.description: Mobile push without an SDK: the Expo Push Service relays to FCM (Android) and APNs (iOS) from one HTTP call. Pure and dependency-free: batches by 100, never throws, reports the dead tokens to forget.

modules.name: @krizaka/realtime
modules.description: Realtime for Node apps behind one interface: a bus (publish / subscribe by channel) and presence (who is connected, by heartbeat and TTL), with memory, PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY and Redis / Valkey adapters, plus Server-Sent Events framing.

modules.name: @krizaka/tailwind
modules.description: The Krizaka Tailwind CSS v4 preset: the semantic --kz-* tokens as utilities (bg-surface-1, text-fg-secondary, border-border-default, text-accent, rounded-xl…), illustration-only light/dark variants and the Krizaka easing.

modules.name: @krizaka/tokens
modules.description: The Krizaka semantic design tokens (--kz-*) and the brand themes (Krizaka, Orazaka, Orochia): one DTCG source compiled to CSS (dark, light, media invariants), typed constants and React Native themes.

modules.name: @krizaka/ui
modules.description: The Krizaka front-end platform's components: the primitives (button, card, dialog, toast, menu, field, tabs, chip, switch, slider, command palette, theme, countdown…) on the semantic --kz-* tokens, the animated marks (Krizaka, Orazaka, Orochia) and the motion signature — web and /native.

modules.name: PostgreSQL (console)
modules.description: The console's own database: its operator account and sessions — never the Orochia data, which it reaches through the admin API.

modules.name: PostgreSQL
modules.description: The Orochia database: accounts, videos, the ledger, auctions, challenges — and the realtime bus (LISTEN/NOTIFY). Schema and migrations in packages/db.

modules.name: Bunny Stream
modules.description: Video storage, encoding and the HLS edge CDN: uploads go to it directly (Tus), playback comes from it with a signed URL.

modules.name: CCBill
modules.description: Card payment gateway: hosted checkout form, signed webhook.

modules.name: Expo Push
modules.description: Push notifications to the iOS and Android app.

modules.name: Facebook sign-in
modules.description: OAuth 2 sign-in: consent dialog, code exchange, profile.

modules.name: Google sign-in
modules.description: OAuth 2 sign-in: consent screen, code exchange, user info.

modules.name: Mailgun
modules.description: Transactional e-mail (verification, password reset, notifications).

modules.name: NowPayments
modules.description: Crypto payment gateway: invoices over its API, signed IPN.

modules.name: Resend
modules.description: Transactional e-mail, the alternative provider.

modules.name: Segpay
modules.description: Card payment gateway: hosted checkout page, signed webhook.

modules.name: Stripe
modules.description: Card payment gateway: Checkout sessions over its API, signed webhook (timestamp tolerance).
